findings.text: RH10 MMR overlay configuration exposes a base region starting at bit 25 spanning 27 bits with mask hex 000ffffffe000000 and an enable at top bit 63 with mask hex 8000000000000000. The generic selector provides that mask and shift only on generation 5 and otherwise yields zero for the mask and minus one for the shift.

The RH10 overlay value is 64 bits with raw access plus identically shaped views for common, YH and generation 5 use. From low to high the layout holds 25 bits of undefined space, a 27-bit writable base, 11 more undefined bits, then a single writable enable at the top.
Address map configuration register address depends on hardware generation, using hex 480000 on generation 4 and hex 1600000 on generations 3 and 2, with zero when none matches.

Address map socket fields have fixed positions. The N socket value starts at bit 6 with a four-bit mask hex 00000000000003c0, while the M socket value starts at bit 0 with a six-bit mask hex 000000000000003f on both generations 3 and 2.

The address map configuration is a 64-bit value with raw access plus generation-specific views. Common and generation 4 views reserve the low six bits and carry a four-bit writable N socket field at bits 6 to 9 with the upper bits reserved. Generation 3 and 2 views instead place a six-bit writable M socket field in the low bits followed by the same four-bit N socket field, with the remainder reserved.

Alias 0 overlay configuration address is hex 4800c8 on generation 4 and hex 16000c8 on generations 3 and 2, else zero. Its base starts at bit 24 with eight-bit mask hex 00000000ff000000, its M alias selector starts at bit 48 with five-bit mask hex 001f000000000000, and its enable is top bit 63 with mask hex 8000000000000000.

Alias 0 overlay is a 64-bit value with raw access and five identically shaped views for common, XH and generations 4, 3 and 2. Low to high it holds 24 reserved bits, an eight-bit writable base, 16 reserved bits, a five-bit writable M alias selector, ten reserved bits, then a single writable enable at the top.

Alias 0 redirect configuration address is hex 4800d0 on generation 4 and hex 16000d0 on generations 3 and 2, else zero. Its destination base starts at bit 24 spanning 22 bits with mask hex 00003fffff000000.

Alias 0 redirect is a 64-bit value with raw access and five identically shaped views. It holds 24 reserved low bits, a 22-bit writable destination base in the middle, and 18 reserved high bits, with no enable field.

Alias 1 overlay configuration address is hex 4800d8 on generation 4 and hex 16000d8 on generations 3 and 2, else zero. Its base starts at bit 24 with eight-bit mask hex 00000000ff000000, its M alias selector starts at bit 48 with five-bit mask hex 001f000000000000, and its enable is top bit 63 with mask hex 8000000000000000.

Alias 1 overlay is a 64-bit value with raw access and five identically shaped views for common, XH and generations 4, 3 and 2. Low to high it holds 24 reserved bits, an eight-bit writable base, 16 reserved bits, a five-bit writable M alias selector, ten reserved bits, then a single writable enable at the top.

Alias 1 redirect configuration address is hex 4800e0 on generation 4 and hex 16000e0 on generations 3 and 2, else zero. Its destination base starts at bit 24 spanning 22 bits with mask hex 00003fffff000000.

Alias 1 redirect is a 64-bit value with raw access and five identically shaped views. It holds 24 reserved low bits, a 22-bit writable destination base in the middle, and 18 reserved high bits, with no enable field.

Alias 2 overlay configuration address is hex 4800e8 on generation 4 and hex 16000e8 on generations 3 and 2, else zero. Its base starts at bit 24 with eight-bit mask hex 00000000ff000000, its M alias selector starts at bit 48 with five-bit mask hex 001f000000000000, and its enable is top bit 63 with mask hex 8000000000000000.

Alias 2 overlay is a 64-bit value with raw access and five identically shaped views for common, XH and generations 4, 3 and 2. Low to high it holds 24 reserved bits, an eight-bit writable base, 16 reserved bits, a five-bit writable M alias selector, ten reserved bits, then a single writable enable at the top.

Alias 2 redirect configuration address is hex 4800f0 on generation 4 and hex 16000f0 on generations 3 and 2, else zero. Its destination base starts at bit 24 spanning 22 bits with mask hex 00003fffff000000.

Alias 2 redirect is a 64-bit value with raw access and five identically shaped views. It holds 24 reserved low bits, a 22-bit writable destination base in the middle, and 18 reserved high bits, with no enable field.

GRU overlay configuration address is hex 480010 on generation 4 and hex 1600010 on generations 3 and 2, else zero. The common N GRU selector starts at bit 52 with four-bit mask hex 00f0000000000000 and the enable is top bit 63 with mask hex 8000000000000000.

GRU overlay base position and width vary by generation. Generation 4A uses shift 26 with mask hex 000ffffffc000000, generation 4 uses shift 26 with mask hex 00003ffffc000000, generations 3 and 2 use shift 28 with mask hex 00003ffff0000000, and generation 3 adds a mode at bit 62 with mask hex 4000000000000000. The generic mask selector covers 4A, 4, 3 and 2 while the generic shift selector lists 4, 3 and 2, falling back to zero and minus one respectively.

GRU overlay is a 64-bit value with raw access and six views whose base region differs. Common views expose only the four-bit writable N GRU selector near the top and the top enable with the rest reserved. Generation 4A pairs a 26-bit writable base with N GRU and enable after 25 reserved low bits plus one undefined bit. Generation 4 uses a 20-bit writable base in the same area with surrounding reserved bits. Generations 3 and 2 use an 18-bit writable base starting at bit 28, with generation 3 adding a writable mode bit next to enable while generation 2 reserves those bits.
High MMIO overlay configuration address is only defined on generation 2 as hex 1600030 and is zero otherwise.

Address selectors evaluate generation predicates in order and fall back to zero when no generation matches, while base shift selectors fall back to minus one. Callers must therefore confirm a supported generation before using the resulting address or shift.

All functional register fields shown are marked writable, while remaining bit ranges are explicitly marked reserved or undefined and carry no defined value. Implementations must not rely on reserved or undefined bits when composing register values.

Using a generic address or shift result without a generation guard risks accessing address zero or shifting by minus one. Writing nonzero values into reserved or undefined ranges risks undefined hardware behavior since the fragments define no effect for those bits.

Overlay configuration registers consistently place their enable in the top bit, while redirect configuration registers expose only a destination base and have no enable. Alias overlay instances 0 through 2 share identical field positions and differ only in register address, as do alias redirect instances 0 through 2.
